title: PHOTONICS-BASED OPTICAL APERTURE FOR LASER COMMUNICATION TERMINALS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5F.056) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a thin optical aperture leveraging advances in integrated photonic technology to reduce the size andweight of space-based optical communication terminals.TargetedImprovements:Reduction of both size and weight of satellite laser communication terminals by 50%.Description: Optical communication terminal solutions with lower size and weight are required to serve the increasing role of small spacecraft for satellitecommercialisation by maximising the amountof payload space for mission-enabling processing or sensors. State-of-the-art optical communicationterminals are often too bulky and heavy for such small platforms and a leap in technology is required. This activity will seek innovative integrated photonicsolutions to replace the telescope subsystem of an optical communication terminal and eliminate as much as possible the need for free-space propagationinside the laser terminal. By doing so, it is expected to greatly reduce the size and inertial mass of the telescope subsystem, enabling for instance furtherreductions in steering assembly size, weight and power.This activity will design and prototype a photonic aperture (or flat telescope) that shall provide good beam quality (for coupling/emitting into/from singlemode waveguides such as single-mode fibres), shall be relatively large (at least several cm in diameter) or provide enough optical gain to enable convincingreplacement of conventional beam expansion and free-space propagation optics (traditional telescope assemblies) in space optical communicationterminals. A foundry-compatible fabrication process of the photonic aperture shall also provide a low-cost telescope alternative by eliminating the need forexpensive optics and assembly and alignment touch labour.The following tasks are envisioned:- Identify the potential solutions and latest innovations in integrated photonic able to replace conventional optical aperture assemblies in space-basedoptical communications for small platforms and/or use cases where accommodation of optical communication terminals is drastically constrained bytheir size and weight.- Develop a preliminary design and expected performance of the chosen solution.- Manufacture and test a prototype and evaluate the performance in a representative laboratory environment.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: QUANTUM COMPUTING ALGORITHMS DEVELOPMENT FOR SPACE APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop and assess quantum computing algorithms, methods and related tools for solving specific spacerelated computational challenges with higher performance and reliability than the state of the art achieved with the classical technologies.Description:Quantum computing technologies are progressing rapidly, with early-stage commercial and academicplatforms offering capabilities relevant to space applications. As one of the strategic sectors expected to benefit from quantum advantage, the space domain offers complex, high-impact challenges that can guide algorithm development and platform requirements. Lessons learned from these applications will be transferable to other sectors, enabling a broader quantum technology ecosystem. This activity aims to ensure European industry is quantum-ready and positioned to lead in the global race for space-enabled quantum technologies. It supports European strategic autonomy by fostering sovereign capabilities in quantum algorithm development, hybrid integration, and secure processing architectures tailored to ESA or national mission needs. The initiative also strengthens Europe's industrial competitiveness by enabling use-case-driven innovation and demonstrating technical leadership in both terrestrial and space environments. This activity aimsto encourage the usage of quantum computing potentials to address the challenges in space missions and technologies. It is expectedto extensively use the precision and fast calculations to solve in the most innovative ways challenges related to, mission planningbooks, AI integration, cryptography, and onboard processing, optimisation algorithm for power batteries, among others. Technology focus areas can include but are not limited to quantum-enhanced simulation for propulsion, materials, thermal, power, satellite station keeping, radiation and orbital dynamics, optimization of tools for mission planning, routing, scheduling, debris avoidance and predictive maintenance, quantum Machine Learning (QML) for Earth Observation, anomaly detection, and FDIR, design of quantumnativepre-measurement processing flows, leveraging intrinsic quantum dynamics to condition mission-criticaldata within the quantum domainpriorto readout or classical interface, digital twin powered by quantumcomputing.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Development and benchmarking of quantum algorithms tailored to space-relevant challengesconsidering gate-based, annealing or hybridquantum computing methods- Ground-based demonstrators for performance validation on quantum computers and/or classical high performance computers- Development of a software tool or product enabling the exploitation of the quantum algorithm for oneor more specific space related use cases- Analysis of the expected performance scaling with future generations of quantum computersThe tasks shall include clearly defined use cases and assess how quantum approachesincluding hybridmethods and error mitigation techniquesperformunder realistic computational loads and spaceenvironments, compared to classical baselines.Deliverables: Software, Report

description: The ESA Fiducial Reference Measurement (FRM) Atlas is an Earth Observation initiative led by to develop an open-access platform forFRM and calibration/validationknowledge.FRMs are fully characterised, traceable measurements with documented uncertainties, used to assess the accuracy and quality of satellite products.ESA-supported FRM activities cover domains including ocean colour, altimetry, surface temperature, atmospheric composition, vegetation, soil moisture and radar.As their associated datasets, procedures and expertise are distributed across many platforms, a centralised mechanism is needed to improve accessibility and interoperability.TheAtlas will provide a single entry point for discovering FRM projects, datasets, procedures, campaigns, documentation, infrastructures and experts.It will connect FRMs with satellite missions, products, variables and validation methodologies,while federating existing resources rather than duplicating them.Its objectives are to improve discoverability, support best practices, promote knowledge reuse and harmonisation, and maximise the value of ESA's Cal/Val investments.

title: STUDY OF CELL-BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF AUTOPHAGY DEVELOPMENT UNDER MICROGRAVITY CONDITIONS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF TECHNOLOGIES FOR PRODUCING ESTABLISHED PLANT PRODUCTS ON SPACE PLATFORMS - EXPRO PLUS
description: Plants are expected to contribute to future exploration systems by providing food, biological resources and regenerative functions during long-duration missions. However, altered-gravity environments can affect plant growth, development, intracellular transport, stress signalling and resource allocation. Autophagy and programmed cell death are conserved cellular processes involved in the degradation and recycling of cellular components and in the regulation of plant development and stress adaptation. Their interaction with cytoskeletal organisation and metabolic regulation may therefore influence the capacity of plants to maintain stable growth and productivity under space-relevant conditions. The objective of the activity is to improve understanding of the cellular and molecular mechanisms that govern plant adaptation to altered-gravity conditions and to translate this knowledge into recommendations supporting reliable plant-based biological production on future space platforms.
